findings.source_quote: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ τῶν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ δεδομένων λαβεῖν τι ἠθέλησεν
findings.english_quote: but did not even wish to receive anything that he offered.
findings.issue: The perfect passive δεδομένων describes the things as given by him. “Offered” silently resolves their relationship to the preceding conditional promise and obscures the sequence of gift-language: δώσω, δεδομένων, and ἀποδοθέντων. The notes discuss pronoun referents but do not disclose this change.
findings.suggested_revision: Use wording such as “but did not even wish to take anything of what had been given by him.” If the things are understood contextually as offered gifts, explain that interpretation while preserving the supplied wording “given” in a note. The revised wording requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: ἐν δὲ τῷ ἐσομένῳ αἰῶνι αἰδίῳ κολασθήσεσθε πυρί
findings.english_quote: while in the coming age you will be punished with eternal fire.
findings.issue: The main rendering defensibly attaches αἰδίῳ to πυρί across the intervening verb, but the notes do not disclose its possible attachment to αἰῶνι. That alternative locates the explicit qualification “eternal” on the coming age rather than on the fire, a material distinction concerning the punishment language.
findings.suggested_revision: The main rendering may remain, but add a note preserving the alternative “in the eternal age to come you will be punished with fire.” Explain that αἰδίῳ agrees in case with either noun and that the chosen reading takes αἰδίῳ … πυρί as an adjective–noun phrase spanning the verb. This is an interpretive attachment issue, not evidence of source corruption; the amended passage requires fresh review.
